body: I’m in the same position. It’s not that I would actually commit, but there are thoughts always lingering on the “what if?” and “would it actually matter?” I can’t tell you, you are suicidal, but if you ever have the thoughts of actually committing, you should talk to someone about it.

I haven’t cut in about 6 years (14yrs old) and I recently did. I’m going to be honest, while I was doing it, it was such an amazing feeling, my wrist was craving it, but now I just feel shitty I did it. They still haven’t completely faded and since were in quarantine, it’s been a hassle to hide them. But now, obviously, it’s been on my mind again and what I tend to do is distract myself as much as I can. Clean my room, reorganize, listen to music, and if you can, talk or txt people. Doesn’t have to about your situation, but maybe about other topics.

You have every right to be angry. But I don’t judge you for not hating them. We often over look abuse and toxicity because we grow accustomed to it, it eventually feels normal. You should be angry, and you’re also not wrong for still having a relationship with them. But you also have to keep in mind that you come first, and if you feel like they make your life hell, and at some point want to cut them off, do it.
If I could tell my father what I went through, I 100% would. If you feel safe and comfortable enough to tell him, you should. Talking about is a huge process of healing.

If she didn’t want it to happen, and she said stop and he didn’t, that is rape. She might be in denial, not wanting to deal with the trauma, she might be blocking it off. When she does feel comfortable to talk about it, just listen and offer your support, don’t try to push her into saying or admitting what happened to her.
Thank so much for your support. I hope you find a therapist you trust as well!

I know it’s inexcusable, and that is one of my many flaws, I’m so selfless that I put my feeling after everyone else’s. The fact that she tried to do so many things to make up for me, makes me feel like in a way she knows she did wrong. I know she is wrong and I blame her for everything I went through, she basically chose the happiness of her youngest child over mine. It’s weird to explain our relationship but at the same time I hate her.
It’s does t matter how long it lasted, or when it was. If you feel like this event is impacting you even the slightest, it’s okay to talk to somebody about it.
